families.name: cursorvault
families.summary: Implement deterministic cursor pagination as a Python 3.11+ standard-library package.

constraints.text: use only the Python standard library

rules.text: create an importable cursorvault package exposing paginate and CursorError from cursorvault.public
paginate(records, cursor=None, limit=3) accepts records with unique string id fields and returns a new dict with exactly items, next_cursor, and has_more; items retain input order
limit must be an integer from 1 through 100 inclusive; booleans are not integers for this contract
{{cursor_rule}}
has_more is true exactly when records remain after the returned page; next_cursor follows R4 when has_more is true and is null otherwise; an empty input returns an empty terminal page
do not mutate records or any record dict, and repeated calls with equal inputs return equal results

done_when.text: the public API imports and can paginate a valid record list in a clean Python 3.11 environment

examples.text: paginate([{id: a}, {id: b}, {id: c}], null, 2) → {{first_page}}
{{second_page_example}}
limit 0 or true → ValueError
any valid records and arguments → records remain unchanged after paginate
{{invalid_cursor_example}}
inspect the cursorvault package dependencies → every imported dependency is from the Python standard library or cursorvault itself

errors.text: invalid limit → raise ValueError without modifying records
malformed or unknown cursor → raise CursorError without modifying records

values.cursor_rule: a non-null cursor is the id of the last record already returned, so the next page begins after that record; when more records remain, next_cursor is the id of the last record in the current page
values.first_page: {items: [{id: a}, {id: b}], next_cursor: b, has_more: true}
values.second_page_example: paginate([{id: a}, {id: b}, {id: c}], b, 2) → {items: [{id: c}], next_cursor: null, has_more: false}

values.cursor_rule: a non-null cursor is the id of the first record to return, so that record is included; when more records remain, next_cursor is the id of the first record not returned in the current page
values.first_page: {items: [{id: a}, {id: b}], next_cursor: c, has_more: true}
values.second_page_example: paginate([{id: a}, {id: b}, {id: c}], b, 2) → {items: [{id: b}, {id: c}], next_cursor: null, has_more: false}

values.cursor_rule: a non-null cursor is the decimal zero-based index of the first record to return; when records remain, next_cursor is the decimal index immediately after the page
values.second_page_example: paginate([{id: a}, {id: b}, {id: c}], "1", 2) → {items: [{id: b}, {id: c}], next_cursor: null, has_more: false}

families.name: configweave
families.summary: Implement immutable recursive configuration merging as a Python 3.11+ standard-library package.

constraints.text: use only the Python standard library

rules.text: create an importable configweave package exposing merge_layers from configweave.public
merge_layers(layers) applies layer dicts from first to last and returns an empty dict for an empty layer list
when both old and new values are mappings, merge recursively; otherwise the later non-list value replaces the earlier value
{{list_rule}}
a later null value deletes that key from the result at its current nesting level; deleting an absent key is a no-op
return a deep copy with no mutable container shared with any input, and never mutate an input layer
layers must be a list of dicts and every key at every nesting level must be a string

done_when.text: the public API imports and can merge valid nested layers in a clean Python 3.11 environment

examples.text: merge_layers([{db: {host: a, port: 1}}, {db: {port: 2}}]) → {db: {host: a, port: 2}}
merge_layers([{plugins: [a, b]}, {plugins: [b, c]}]) → {{list_result}}
merge_layers([{a: 1, b: 2}, {a: null}]) → {b: 2}
any valid layers → mutating the result cannot mutate a source layer and source layers remain unchanged
a non-dict layer or nested non-string key → TypeError
inspect the configweave package dependencies → every imported dependency is from the Python standard library or configweave itself

errors.text: invalid layer structure or any non-string key → raise TypeError without mutating inputs

values.list_rule: when a later value is a list, replace the earlier value with a deep copy of that list
when both old and new values are lists, concatenate deep copies in old-then-new order; a list still replaces a non-list
when both old and new values are lists, concatenate in old-then-new order while keeping only the first occurrence of each equality-distinct value; a list still replaces a non-list

families.name: idledger
families.summary: Implement an idempotent in-memory account ledger as a Python 3.11+ standard-library package.

constraints.text: balances and command amounts are integer cents and no successful operation may leave a negative balance
use only the Python standard library

rules.text: create an importable idledger package exposing Ledger, InsufficientFunds, and CommandConflict from idledger.public
Ledger(initial=None) accepts a mapping of account names to non-negative integer balances; snapshot returns a new account-name-sorted dict
apply(command) accepts exactly id, account, kind, and amount where kind is credit or debit and amount is a positive integer; a success returns exactly id, account, and resulting balance
repeating an identical successful command id returns the original result without applying the command again
{{conflict_rule}}
a debit that would make a balance negative raises InsufficientFunds, leaves all state unchanged, and does not consume the command id
invalid initial state or command structure raises ValueError and leaves all state and command history unchanged
apply and snapshot are thread-safe; concurrent successful commands are each reflected exactly once

done_when.text: the public API imports and can apply a valid command in a clean Python 3.11 environment

examples.text: Ledger({a: 100}).apply({id: c1, account: a, kind: debit, amount: 40}) → {id: c1, account: a, balance: 60}
applying the same successful command twice → the second result equals the first and the balance changes once
{{conflict_example}}
debit 101 from balance 100 → InsufficientFunds and the command id remains reusable
amount true, zero, or a command with extra fields → ValueError and no state change
concurrent distinct credits → final balance equals the initial balance plus every credit exactly once
inspect the idledger package dependencies → every imported dependency is from the Python standard library or idledger itself

errors.text: invalid initial state or command → raise ValueError atomically

values.conflict_rule: reusing a successful command id with different command content raises CommandConflict and leaves the original result and all balances unchanged
values.conflict_example: reuse c1 with different content → CommandConflict and the original state remains

values.conflict_rule: reusing a successful command id with different command content returns the original result and leaves balances unchanged; the first successful command wins
values.conflict_example: reuse c1 with different content → return the original c1 result and retain the original state

values.conflict_rule: a conflicting successful command id atomically replaces the original: reverse the original, apply and return the replacement, or preserve the original if replacement fails
values.conflict_example: replace c1 debit 40 with c1 credit 20 → reverse the debit, apply the credit, and return balance 120

families.name: tokenquota
families.summary: Implement a thread-safe clock-driven token bucket as a Python 3.11+ standard-library package.

constraints.text: use only the supplied clock for elapsed-time decisions and use only the Python standard library

rules.text: create an importable tokenquota package exposing Bucket from tokenquota.public; Bucket(capacity, refill_per_second, clock=None) starts full
allow(amount=1) refills first, consumes amount and returns true when enough tokens exist, otherwise returns false without consuming
refill adds elapsed_seconds times refill_per_second, never exceeds capacity, and treats a backward clock movement as zero elapsed time
{{rounding_rule}}
available() performs the same refill calculation and returns the current numeric balance without consuming tokens
constructor capacity must be positive, refill_per_second non-negative, and allow amount positive and not boolean; invalid values raise ValueError
allow and available are thread-safe so concurrent successful consumption never exceeds available tokens

done_when.text: the public API imports and can consume from a valid bucket in a clean Python 3.11 environment

examples.text: a capacity-2 bucket at time 0 → allow(1) is true twice and then false
after emptying a capacity-3 bucket with refill rate 0.5 and advancing 3 seconds → available() is {{rounded_value}}
advancing far beyond capacity or moving the clock backward → balance never exceeds capacity and never gains tokens from negative elapsed time
capacity 0, negative refill, or allow(true) → ValueError
many concurrent allow(1) calls against a full capacity-N bucket with no refill → exactly N calls succeed
supply a fake clock and inspect package dependencies → the fake clock fully controls refill and only standard-library dependencies appear

errors.text: invalid constructor or consumption amount → raise ValueError without consuming tokens

values.rounding_rule: preserve fractional tokens exactly after refill; do not round the balance
after each positive-time refill and capacity clamp, round the balance down to the nearest integer before answering the operation
after each positive-time refill and capacity clamp, round the balance up to the nearest integer without exceeding capacity before answering the operation

families.name: wirecodec
families.summary: Implement a deterministic versioned JSON wire codec as a Python 3.11+ standard-library package.

constraints.text: use only the Python standard library and SHA-256 from hashlib

baseline.reference: version 1 JSON records containing id and value with no checksum

preserve.text: decode version 1 records where version is absent or equals 1
the public encode, decode, and CodecError imports remain stable

evolve.text: encode deterministic version 2 records with a checksum
decode version 2 records only when the checksum is valid

rules.text: create an importable wirecodec package exposing encode, decode, and CodecError from wirecodec.public
encode(record) requires exactly a non-empty string id and an integer non-boolean value, does not mutate record, and raises ValueError for invalid input
encode returns compact JSON with sorted object keys containing version 2, id, value, and checksum; checksum is lowercase SHA-256 hex over compact sorted JSON of only id, value, and version
decode(text) accepts a JSON object string, treats absent version as version 1, and returns a new dict containing id, value, and version
decode validates version 2 checksum before returning and raises CodecError for malformed JSON, unsupported versions, invalid fields, or checksum mismatch
{{unknown_rule}}
equal inputs produce byte-for-byte equal encoded strings across repeated calls

done_when.text: the public API imports and can encode a valid record in a clean Python 3.11 environment

examples.text: encode({id: a, value: 2}) → compact version 2 JSON whose checksum matches its canonical known-field payload
decode("{\"id\":\"a\",\"value\":2}") → {id: a, value: 2, version: 1}
decode(a valid encoded version 2 record) → {id: a, value: 2, version: 2}
decode a valid record with unknown field note=ok → {{unknown_result}}
decode version 2 with a changed value but original checksum → CodecError
repeated encode of the same valid record → identical bytes and no input mutation
encode missing id or with boolean value → ValueError
inspect wirecodec dependencies and a produced checksum → only standard-library imports are used and the digest is SHA-256

errors.text: invalid encode input → raise ValueError without mutating input
malformed, unsupported, or checksum-invalid wire input → raise CodecError

values.unknown_rule: when decoding version 1 or 2, discard unknown top-level fields after validating known fields
values.unknown_result: return only {id, value, version}; note is absent

values.unknown_rule: when decoding version 1 or 2, any unknown top-level field raises CodecError
when decoding version 1 or 2, preserve unknown top-level fields in an extras dict in the returned record; extras is omitted when empty

families.name: detreport
families.summary: Implement deterministic aggregate report generation as a Python 3.11+ standard-library package and CLI.

constraints.text: amounts and totals are integer cents and use only the Python standard library

stable.text: the complete report string is byte-for-byte stable for the same ordered input

rules.text: create an importable detreport package exposing build_report and ReportError from detreport.public plus python -m detreport INPUT_JSON
each event must be a dict with exactly unique non-empty string id, non-empty string category, and integer non-boolean amount_cents; invalid input raises ReportError
group events by category into objects with exactly category, count, total_cents, and events; events is the list of event ids sorted ascending
return compact ensure_ascii=false JSON with sorted object keys and exactly groups plus grand_total_cents at the top level
{{order_rule}}
grand_total_cents is the sum of every event amount and input events are never mutated
the CLI reads a JSON array from the supplied path, prints exactly build_report output plus one newline, and exits successfully

done_when.text: the public API imports and can build a valid single-category report in a clean Python 3.11 environment

examples.text: events [{id: b, category: x, amount_cents: 2}, {id: a, category: x, amount_cents: -1}] → group x has count 2, total_cents 1, events [a, b], and grand total 1
categories encountered as beta then alpha → groups ordered {{order_result}}
category café → output contains literal café rather than an ASCII escape
duplicate ids, boolean amount, missing field, or extra field → ReportError
repeating build_report on the same ordered events → identical bytes and unchanged input
python -m detreport input.json → stdout is the library result followed by one newline
inspect the detreport package dependencies → every imported dependency is from the Python standard library or detreport itself

errors.text: invalid event collection or event → raise ReportError without mutating input

values.order_rule: order group objects by category in ascending Unicode code-point order
order group objects by category in descending Unicode code-point order
order group objects by the first appearance of each category in the input sequence
